candidates.comment: A repeal relation between two pieces of legislation, where one cancels or abrogates the other. Also called: cancels, abrogates, revokes. Examples: "New Act legislationRepeals Old Act", "Regulation X legislationRepeals Directive Y", "Law 123 legislationRepeals Statute 456".

candidates.label: suitableForDiet
candidates.comment: An indication of a dietary restriction or guideline for which a recipe or menu item is appropriate. Also called "dietary suitability", "dietary compliance", "dietary restriction friendly", "accommodates diet". Examples: "The recipe is suitableForDiet VeganDiet", "The menu item's suitableForDiet is GlutenFreeDiet", "This dish is suitableForDiet HalalDiet."

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: ineligibleRegion
candidates.comment: A geographical exclusion relation between an action access specification, delivery charge specification, demand, media object, or offer, and the region where it is not valid or available. Also called restricted region, excluded region, unavailable in, not valid in. Examples: An offer has an ineligibleRegion of 'Alaska'. A delivery charge specification has an ineligibleRegion of 'Hawaii'. A media object has an ineligibleRegion of 'EU'. Distinct from eligibleRegion, which specifies where something *is* valid or available.

chosen_property.label: represents
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that an organization represents an administrative area.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property for representation between these types; minting.

candidates.label: item
candidates.comment: A list element relation between a data feed item or list item and the entity it represents within a collection. Also called represents, refers to, entry, element. Examples: A list item has an item of 'John Doe'. A data feed item has an item of 'Product X'. A list entry has an item of 'Event Y'.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: encoding
candidates.comment: An encoding relation between a creative work and a media object that represents or contains it. Also called "represented by media", "media representation", "has media object". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encoding 'Matrix.mp4'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encoding 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3'", "Book '1984' encoding '1984.epub'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: encodings
candidates.comment: An encodings relation between a creative work and the media objects that represent or contain it. Also called "represented by media objects", "has media representations", "media versions". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encodings 'Matrix.mp4', 'Matrix.avi'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encodings 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3', 'BohemianRhapsody.wav'", "Book '1984' encodings '1984.epub', '1984.pdf'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: encodesCreativeWork
candidates.comment: An encodes creative work relation between a media object and the creative work it represents or contains. Also called "represents work", "contains work", "media of work". Examples: "Video file encodesCreativeWork 'Movie Title'", "Audio recording encodesCreativeWork 'Song Title'", "Image file encodesCreativeWork 'Painting Title'". Distinct from encoding, which is the inverse relation (CreativeWork -> MediaObject).

candidates.label: representativeOfPage
candidates.comment: A representative of page relation indicating whether an image object accurately reflects the content of the web page it appears on. Also called page representative, content summary image. Examples: "A thumbnail image is representative of page 'true'.", "A decorative image is representative of page 'false'.", "A product photo is representative of page 'true'."

candidates.label: tickerSymbol
candidates.comment: A textual identifier representing the exchange-traded instrument associated with a corporation, typically an exchange and instrument name. Also called "stock symbol", "stock ticker", "exchange symbol", "trading symbol". Examples: "Apple Inc. has tickerSymbol NASDAQ AAPL", "The corporation's tickerSymbol is NYSE GOOG", "This company is identified by its tickerSymbol."

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: logo
candidates.comment: A logo relation between a brand, certification, organization, place, product, or service and its associated image or URL. Also called: brand logo, official emblem, corporate identity. Examples: "Apple Inc. logo Apple Logo Image", "Nike Product logo Nike Swoosh", "Olympic Games logo Olympic Rings".

candidates.label: photo
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to a single photograph depicting it. Also called image, picture, visual representation. Examples: A restaurant has a photo of its interior. A park has a photo of its main entrance. A landmark has a photo of its facade. Distinct from photos, which links to multiple photographs.

chosen_property.label: worksFor
chosen_property.justification: worksFor directly matches employment relation.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: practicesAt
candidates.comment: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.

candidates.label: workLocation
candidates.comment: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: workPresented
candidates.comment: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.

candidates.label: exampleOfWork
candidates.comment: An example relation between a creative work and another creative work that it is an instance, realization, or derivation of. Also called: instance of, realization of, derivation of, based on. Examples: "Mona Lisa (print)" example of work "Mona Lisa (original painting)", "Hamlet (film)" example of work "Hamlet (play)", "Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)" example of work "Star Wars: A New Hope (film)".

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: workHours
candidates.comment: A work hours relation between a job posting and a text description, specifying the typical schedule or shifts for the position. Also called working schedule, shift pattern, typical hours. Examples: JobPosting workHours "9am-5pm, Mon-Fri", JobPosting workHours "Night Shift", JobPosting workHours "Flexible".

candidates.label: creativeWorkStatus
candidates.comment: A lifecycle stage relation between a creative work and its current status. Also called: work status, publication status, development stage. Examples: "Draft Novel" creative work status "Draft", "Published Article" creative work status "Published", "Archived Website" creative work status "Obsolete", "In-progress Film" creative work status "Incomplete".

chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property for providing data for an export; minting.

candidates.label: supportingData

Examples: "The mapping application has supportingData a traffic data feed", "The software application's supportingData is a weather feed", "This program uses supportingData for real-time updates."

candidates.label: providesService
candidates.comment: A service provision relation between a service channel and the specific service it delivers. Also called channel delivers, service offered via, offers service. Examples: "An online portal provides service 'customer support'.", "A phone line provides service 'technical assistance'.", "A mobile app provides service 'online banking'."

candidates.label: healthcareReportingData
candidates.comment: A healthcare reporting data relation between a hospital and its associated reporting data, such as CDC records or datasets. Examples: "A hospital has healthcare reporting data from the CDC.", "The hospital provides healthcare reporting data as a dataset.", "This facility publishes its healthcare reporting data."

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: dataset
candidates.comment: A containment relation between a data catalog and a dataset included within it. Also called: cataloged dataset, included dataset, data collection. Examples: "Government Data Catalog" dataset "Population Census 2020", "Research Data Repository" dataset "Climate Change Projections", "Open Data Portal" dataset "Public Transport Schedules".

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

candidates.label: sdPublisher
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for generating and publishing the structured data markup for a creative work. Also called structured data provider, metadata publisher, data markup creator. Examples: `Article Structured Data` sdPublisher `Schema.org Generator`, `Open Data Project` sdPublisher `University Research Group`, `Student Project` sdPublisher `Jane Doe`. Distinct from `publisher`, which is the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: evidenceOrigin
candidates.comment: An evidence origin relation between a medical guideline and the source of data used to formulate it. Also called: data source, guideline source, origin of evidence. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" evidence origin "RCT", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" evidence origin "Consensus Opinion", "WHO Guideline for COVID-19" evidence origin "Observational Studies". Distinct from evidenceLevel, which is the strength of the evidence.

candidates.label: schoolClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: Information regarding school closures, typically provided as a URL or web content within a special announcement. Also called school closing details, closure announcement, education disruption info. Examples: `Emergency Announcement` schoolClosuresInfo `URL to district website`, `Weather Alert` schoolClosuresInfo `Text about snow day`, `Public Health Notice` schoolClosuresInfo `WebContent on school status`.

chosen_property.label: publisher
chosen_property.justification: publisher expresses the organization that publishes a report.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: publication
candidates.comment: A publication relation between a creative work and the event of its publication. Also called published as, associated publication event. Examples: "A book has a publication event in 2023.", "A research paper has a publication event in a journal.", "A song has a publication event as a single."

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: publishingPrinciples
candidates.comment: A publishing principles relation between a creative work, organization, or person and the document outlining their editorial and ethical guidelines as a publisher. Also called editorial guidelines, ethics policy, publishing policy. Examples: "A news organization has publishing principles outlined on its website.", "A research journal adheres to specific publishing principles.", "A blogger follows certain publishing principles for their content."

candidates.label: publicationType
candidates.comment: A publication type relation between a medical scholarly article and its classification according to a catalog like MeSH. Also called article type, MeSH type. Examples: "A medical article has a publication type 'Review'.", "A research paper has a publication type 'Clinical Trial'.", "A case study has a publication type 'Case Report'."

candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". candidates.label: printEdition
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific edition of a print product in which a news article is published. Also called edition name, print version, publication edition. Examples: A news article appears in print edition 'Late City Edition'. The story is in print edition 'National Edition'. The article's print edition is 'Weekend Edition'.

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: bookFormat
candidates.comment: A type of book format for a book. Also called: publication format, book binding. Examples: "Book 'Novel' bookFormat 'BookFormatType.Hardcover'", "Book 'Ebook' bookFormat 'BookFormatType.EBook'."

candidates.label: publisherImprint
candidates.comment: A publisher imprint relation between a creative work and the specific publishing division or imprint responsible for its release. Also called imprint of, published under imprint. Examples: "A comic book has a publisher imprint 'Vertigo Comics'.", "A novel has a publisher imprint 'Vintage Books'.", "A children's book has a publisher imprint 'Puffin Books'."

chosen_property.label: hasIndustry
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the industry or product group that an entity is associated with.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property for a country having an industry; minting.

candidates.label: industry
candidates.comment: An industry classification relation between a job posting and the sector of economic activity it belongs to. Also called sector, business area, field, domain. Examples: A software engineer job posting has an industry of 'Technology'. A nurse job posting has an industry of 'Healthcare'. A marketing manager job posting has an industry of 'Advertising'.

candidates.label: hasPOS
candidates.comment: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point. Examples: "An organization has a POS in New York.", "The vendor has a POS at the market.", "This company operates multiple POS locations."

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: hasShippingService
candidates.comment: A shipping service relation between offer shipping details or an organization and a shipping service it provides. Also called offers shipping, shipping option, delivery service. Examples: "An organization has a shipping service for international delivery.", "Offer shipping details include a shipping service for express mail.", "The company provides a shipping service."

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: isicV4
candidates.comment: An industry classification relation between an organization, person, or place and its International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 4 code. Also called ISIC code, industry classification code, economic activity code. Examples: An organization has an isicV4 of '6201' (Computer programming activities). A person has an isicV4 of '8620' (Medical and dental practice activities). A place has an isicV4 of '5510' (Hotels and similar accommodation).

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: hasMeasurement
candidates.comment: A measurement relation between a certification, offer, product, or size specification and a quantitative value representing a specific measurement. Also called item measurement, dimension, size value. Examples: "A product has a measurement for its height.", "An offer includes a measurement for package weight.", "The certification has a measurement of carbon footprint."

chosen_property.label: hasRivalryWith
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the entity with which there is a rivalry.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property for rivalry between countries; minting.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: hasSponsorshipOffer
candidates.comment: A sponsorship offer relation between an event and an offer to sponsor it. Also called sponsorship opportunity, sponsor package, call for sponsors. Examples: "An event has a sponsorship offer for corporate partners.", "The conference has a sponsorship offer with different tiers.", "This festival includes a sponsorship offer.". candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: sibling
candidates.comment: A familial relationship between two people who share at least one parent. Also called brother, sister, kin, family member. Examples: `John Doe` sibling `Jane Doe`, `Mary Smith` sibling `Tom Smith`, `Alice Brown` sibling `Bob Brown`. Distinct from `siblings`, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". chosen_property.label: trails

candidates.label: breadcrumb
candidates.comment: A set of links that helps a user understand and navigate a website hierarchy on a webpage. Also called: breadcrumb trail, navigation path, site path. Examples: "WebPage 'Product Page' breadcrumb 'Home > Category > Product'", "WebPage 'Article' breadcrumb 'Blog > Year > Month > Article Title'."

candidates.label: exerciseCourse
candidates.comment: An exercise course relation between an exercise action and the specific place or course where the action was performed. Also called: workout location, training venue, activity course. Examples: "Morning Run" exercise course "Central Park Loop", "Swimming Practice" exercise course "Olympic Pool Lane 3", "Cycling Race" exercise course "Mountain Bike Trail". Distinct from fromLocation, which is the original location before the action.

candidates.label: hasMap
candidates.comment: A map relation between a place and its associated map or map URL. Also called map of, location map, geographical map. Examples: "A restaurant has a map of its location.", "The park has a map showing its trails.", "This place has a map URL."

candidates.label: course
candidates.comment: A location relation between an exercise action and the course where it was performed. Also called: exercise location, training course, activity venue. Examples: "Morning Run" course "Central Park Loop", "Golf Game" course "Augusta National", "Cycling Race" course "Tour de France Route".

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: sensoryUnit
candidates.comment: The neurological pathway or anatomical structure that transmits sensory information to the brain or spinal cord. Also called sensory pathway, afferent pathway, nerve input. candidates.label: distance
candidates.comment: A distance relation between an exercise action or travel action and the length travelled. Also called "travelled distance", "route length", "journey distance". candidates.label: line

candidates.label: itinerary
candidates.comment: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

chosen_property.label: leadsIn
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the product or domain in which an entity leads.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property for leading in a product; minting.

candidates.label: advanceBookingRequirement
candidates.comment: An advance booking requirement relation between a demand or offer and the minimum time needed between acceptance and actual usage. Examples: "A flight offer's advance booking requirement is '24 hours'.", "The concert ticket demand has an advance booking requirement of '7 days'."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: hasPOS
candidates.comment: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point. Examples: "An organization has a POS in New York.", "The vendor has a POS at the market.", "This company operates multiple POS locations."

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: knowsAbout
candidates.comment: A knowledge domain relation between an organization or person and a topic or entity they possess knowledge about. Also called knowledgeable about, familiar with topic, understands, has expertise in (without implying skill level). Examples: A person knowsAbout 'artificial intelligence'. An organization knowsAbout 'renewable energy policy'. A researcher knowsAbout 'quantum physics'. Distinct from hasOccupation or alumniOf, which are about formal roles or education, not general knowledge.

candidates.label: hasMemberProgram
candidates.comment: A member program relation between an organization and a member program it offers. Also called offers program, loyalty program, membership program. Examples: "An airline has a member program for frequent flyers.", "An eCommerce merchant has a member program for discounts.", "The organization offers a member program."

chosen_property.label: hasRelationTo
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a general relation between a country and another entity.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property captures this generic relation; minting.

candidates.label: hasMap
candidates.comment: A map relation between a place and its associated map or map URL. Also called map of, location map, geographical map. Examples: "A restaurant has a map of its location.", "The park has a map showing its trails.", "This place has a map URL."

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: relatedStructure
candidates.comment: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.
